html.body: Date: 2025-03-14 REMARKSClaims 1-5 are pending. Claims 1-3 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over US 2020/0231087 to Morimura in view of US 2023/0116572 to Bang. Claims 4-5 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Morimura in view of Bang and further in view of US 2021/0387640 to Tamori. Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the remarks and amendments submitted herewith.Amendments to the Claims Claims 1 and 3-5 have been amended as shown herein. Claims 6-7 are newly added.Independent claim 1 has been amended to replace "controller" with a "processor" and to recite that the degree of automated controllability includes: a first state in which the door is automatically opened or closed based on a control command, a second state in which the door cannot be automatically controlled, and is opened or closed by pressing a button provided in the cabin, and a third state in which the door is not operable, and has to be manually opened or closed.Dependent claims 3-5 has been amended in view of the amendments to independent claim 1.Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures, and claims as originally filed. No subject matter has been disclaimed and the amendment of certain claims is not to be construed as a dedication to the public of any of the subject matter of the claims as previously presented. It is believed that no new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.Summary of Examiner Interview Anubhav Sharma thanks Examiner Staubach for the telephonic interview of February 27, 2025. The claims of the subject application were discussed in view of the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejections. A tentative agreement was reached regarding proposed amendments, which are formally presented herein, to overcome the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejections. However, the Examiner indicated that an updated search and consideration would be required.Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as this statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. §1.133.Acknowledgment of Drawings With respect to the Office Action Summary, Applicant respectfully requests acknowledgment and acceptance of the drawings.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. .103 Claims 1-3 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Morimura in view of Bang. Claims 4-5 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Morimura in view of Bang and further in view of Tamori. The rejection is respectfully traversed.The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62-63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great At. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S. 147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." WL. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert. denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).As tentatively agreed during the interview, Applicant respectfully submits that Morimura in view of Bang fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1.Specifically, Morimura in view of Bang fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1 regarding the degree of automated controllability includes: a first state in which the door is automatically opened or closed based on a control command, a second state in which the door cannot be automatically controlled, and is opened or closed by pressing a button provided in the cabin, and a third state in which the door is not operable, and has to be manually opened or closed.Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claim 1, and its respective dependent claims, can no longer be rejected as being unpatentable over Morimura in view of Bang. Further, Bang and Tamori fail to cure the deficiencies of Morimura.Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.New Dependent Claims 6-7 New dependent claims 6-7 have been added to depend upon independent claim 1.Dependent claim 6 has been newly added to recite the processor is configured to: in the first state, determine that the work by the passenger is not needed, and provide a first notification that passengers in the cabin should wait for the door to open automatically; and in the second or third state, determine that the work by the passenger is needed, and provide a second notification that requests cooperation from the passengers.Dependent claim 7 has been added to recite the processor is configured to: based on determining that there is a passenger who is expected to be able to open or close the door manually, among the one or more passengers of the vehicle, provide a first notification that requests cooperation from the passenger; and based on determining that there is no passenger who is expected to be able to open or close the door manually, among the one or more passengers of the vehicle, provide a second notification that asks the one or more passengers to wait for arrival of help.Given that dependent claims 6-7 depend from independent claim 1, dependent claims 6-7 are patentable over the cited references for at least the reasons presented above with respect to independent claim 1, and for the respective subject matter recited in each of these claims.Entry and consideration of dependent claims 6-7 is respectfully requested.Conclusion In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response.Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.Respectfully submitted, / Anubhav Sharma / Anubhav Sharma Registration No.: 66,434 Attorney for Assignee Dinsmore & Shohl LLP 1001 Lakeside Avenue, Suite 990 Cleveland, OH 44114 (216) 413-3820
